answer: Anyone who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the onyx history. Churn is counted in cedar, and prism publishes the ratio each epoch. At most 9% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. Every extra alias adds 8 hours of verification and 9 percent more locked value. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
